items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I called him Peas. His nickname was Sweetpea, and I one-upped him... I went up to him and said, “Peas, this is just fantastic.”

ctx.x: Billy Strayhorn. What was your memory, recollection of him? And did he do material for you, to try to feature you?

Billy Strayhorn was Duke’s alter-ego. He was an extension of the maestro. The maestro gave him carte-blanche as far as writing and living was concerned. I understand he didn’t even have a salary, that he just did whatever he felt like doing, and Duke of course being backed up with his ASCAP earnings – he got lots of money from ASCAP every year, so he and Strayhorn just lived and paid the expenses with their – his ASCAP earnings.
